Seasonality analysis of a coin

Source: R/fct_seasonality.R
seasonality_analysis.Rd

Do some days of the week, weeks of the year, months or years of the halving cycle bring better returns than others? The returns of the complete periods (see seasonal_returns()) are summed up by group, and a Kruskal-Wallis test asks whether the differences between the groups are larger than chance would give. The test compares the ranks of the returns, so a few extreme months do not decide it, but it takes the returns as independent, which crypto returns are only roughly: calm and wild stretches come in runs.

Usage

seasonality_analysis(history, period = c("day", "week", "month", "year"))

Arguments

history

Price history of one coin from get_history(), with all of it.

period

"day", "week", "month" or "year".

Value

NULL when the history has no complete period with one before it, or a list with:

coin, period

What was analysed.

returns

The returns of seasonal_returns().

groups

A row per group that has returns, in their natural order: group, returns (how many), mean_pct, median_pct, up_pct (the share of the returns above 0), best_pct and worst_pct.

all

The same numbers for all the returns together, as a list.

p_value

The p-value of the Kruskal-Wallis test, NA when fewer than two groups have returns, or no group has two.

Examples

btc <- get_history("Bitcoin (BTC)", as.Date("2013-04-29"))
analysis <- seasonality_analysis(btc, "month")
analysis$groups
#>    group returns   mean_pct median_pct   up_pct   best_pct worst_pct
#> 1    Jan      13 -0.2909088  0.6910592 53.84615  39.835567 -32.08346
#> 2    Feb      13  6.8058464 11.4810969 69.23077  43.716856 -33.81771
#> 3    Mar      13 -0.8480297 -2.1619465 46.15385  30.531110 -32.93329
#> 4    Apr      13  9.2210271  7.5802233 61.53846  34.477899 -17.18056
#> 5    May      14  9.2234063  3.3732947 50.00000  69.628819 -35.35456
#> 6    Jun      14 -1.5659196 -0.5140670 50.00000  26.713348 -37.76883
#> 7    Jul      14  7.7163080  8.1254476 71.42857  23.916334  -8.37172
#> 8    Aug      14  2.3174099 -7.1875290 35.71429  63.576829 -19.17934
#> 9    Sep      14 -2.4603540 -2.4092218 42.85714   7.392924 -19.00922
#> 10   Oct      14 17.5478457 12.9418542 71.42857  53.383459 -12.56590
#> 11   Nov      13 41.8265543  8.7832808 61.53846 453.642183 -36.41158
#> 12   Dec      13  4.0366002 -3.1921079 38.46154  47.773176 -33.23978
analysis$p_value
#> [1] 0.3450331
seasonality_text(analysis)
#> $groups
#> $groups$headline
